Levey-Jennings tracking of URCP-38-2K 6-peak Ultra Rainbow beads on the Cytek Aurora EVO. Last run: 2026-11-10 00:00 (27 runs).

Median column: the Peak 6 tabs show the median of the brightest population for each detector, one tab per laser. The All peaks tabs show all six population medians together (peak 1 = blank) on a log axis, with no control bands.

rCV column: robust %CV of Peak 6 (brightest) and Peak 1 (blank). The blank median sits close to zero, so its %rCV is volatile even when the absolute spread is stable. The noise-floor SD on the main 6-peak page is the more robust blank measure.

Linearity & 2+2SD page. Linearity shows R² of log₁₀(median) against peak number over peaks 2–6 for each detector (1 = perfectly log-linear). The MEF tab shows the log-log slope of median against the certificate MEF values for the 18 certificate detectors (ideal 1, acceptable 0.9–1.1). 2+2SD is the Parks 2018 limit of resolution in MFI for all 64 detectors, where lower means more sensitive. Its MEF tab shows the same limit in MEF units. Detectors marked MEF scale mismatch fail the slope check, so their MEF values are lower-confidence. Runs whose fit failed have no 2+2SD value and are not plotted.

Control bands: every band is centred on the detector’s robust median over the full history, and needs at least 8 unflagged runs.

  • Peak 6 median uses fixed percentage limits: green is within ±3%, amber is 3–5%, and the red dashed lines are the ±5% action limits. Daily QC sets the gain to hold this value at a target, so a fixed tolerance compares across detectors. A typical detector varies by about 1% run to run, so a point past ±5% is a real shift.
  • All other LJ plots (rCV, linearity, 2+2SD) use SD bands: green is within ±2 SD, amber is 2–3 SD, and the red dashed lines are at ±3 SD, where SD is the MAD-scaled SD.
  • All peaks plots have no bands.

Red squares mark runs where that peak was saturated or out of range. They’re plotted but left out of the band baseline. Dotted blue verticals are engineer visits.

Note: daily QC pins bead MFI by adjusting gain, so the medians are held roughly constant by design. Sustained shifts point to a QC-target or gain issue, not directly to detector health. See the Help page for more.

University of Sydney, Australia
